articles.title: Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc hit with Sao Paulo grid penalties in more Ferrari misery
articles.summary: The warring Ferrari duo both changed their engines for the first time this season
articles.body:
Warring Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc will both receive 10-place grid penalties for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix .

The Ferrari duo have both changed their engines for the first time this season and as such have been hit with the penalty by the FIA.

But Hamilton immediately hit trouble in final practice. First he complained of vibrations from his new engine before having to come in again with his car pouring smoke from the back.

He jumped out with 23 minutes remaining as his mechanics began taking his car apart. Hamilton ended the session 12th fastest.

The pair held showdown talks with boss Fred Vasseur on Thursday evening after Hamilton's fury over his team-mate's lap-one overtake on him in Mexico.

Hamilton questioned Leclerc's mentality and vowed not to be silenced at Ferrari as he arrived in Brazil. Vasseur and Leclerc say the matter is settled after those talks.

Their squabble allowed Max Verstappen to win last weekend's race. The Dutchman has risen to second in the standings after victory in three of the last four races but will start from the rear of the grid on Sunday after taking on several new engine components.

It is a position he is familiar with having done the same here over the last two years, famously winning from 17th in the rain in 2024.

Verstappen set the pace in the final session before qualifying, beating new world champion Kimi Antonelli by just 0.025 seconds, with Lando Norris third.

George Russell, who has a five-place grid drop of his own, was fourth ahead of Leclerc.

Rain fell as final practice got under way on Saturday and is forecast across the weekend, with the chance of qualifying and Sunday's race being affected.

Formula One announced a five-year extension for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix ahead of qualifying, confirming its place on the calendar until 2035.

articles.title: Eagles vs. Giants: 5 keys to a Philadelphia victory in Week 9
articles.summary: The Eagles need better protection, a healthier Saquon Barkley and defensive pressure to get past the Giants in Week 9.
articles.body:
It felt like it took forever for the NFL season to arrive, and now, look... It's basically halfway over. It's Week 9, and the Philadelphia Eagles don't need another game in which the quarterback spends more time dealing with pressure than attacking the opposing defense.

At 2-6, Philadelphia has reached a point where every Sunday feels like an examination of how much this team can still salvage from a disappointing season. A matchup with the New York Giants offers an opportunity to change the mood, but the Eagles won't get there by relying on familiar names or expecting things to suddenly fall into place.

Joe Milton gets his first opportunity to help change the trajectory , while the defense faces a quarterback who has given the Giants some unexpected momentum. Philadelphia has enough talent to win this game, but talent alone hasn't been enough lately. Here are five keys that could determine whether the Eagles finally give their fans something to celebrate. It's Eagles vs. Giants , and when these two meet, records are often thrown out the window.

Jalen Carter has to generate consistent interior pressure?

There may not be a more frustrating player on Philadelphia's roster than Jalen Carter, but that's largely because of his potential. He can look like one of the best defensive tackles in football one week and disappear for stretches in the next.

The talent isn't in question. The consistency is. The Eagles need the disruptive version of Carter against New York. His ability to collapse the pocket from the interior can create problems for a quarterback who has shown plenty of confidence throwing downfield.

A dominant Carter can also force the Giants to commit additional resources to the middle of their offensive line, creating opportunities for Philadelphia's edge rushers. It won't be easy. Per Pro Football Focus, he has certainly flashed statistically against the pass rush.

Carter showed life against the Washington Commanders, recording a sack, but one productive afternoon isn't enough to answer the bigger question. Motivated Jalen Carter is a player the Eagles can build their defensive front around. They need that player to show up Sunday.

Saquon Barkley needs a productive workload

A hamstring injury is difficult enough for a running back to overcome. Add a back injury to the equation, and Philadelphia has a legitimate reason to be cautious or even worried.

His availability matters, but so does his ability to handle a workload that can actually influence the game. Barkley has tormented his former team before, and a matchup against New York naturally offers some extra motivation.

More importantly, the Eagles need a dependable running game to take pressure off their quarterback. Their struggles on the ground have contributed to an offense that consistently finds itself in unfavorable situations.

If Barkley is healthy enough to contribute, his presence could change the way the Giants approach Philadelphia's offense. But the Eagles shouldn't confuse having him available with having him ready to carry the entire rushing attack. His effectiveness will matter more than his name on the lineup card.

Vic Fangio must frustrate a suddenly white-hot J.J. McCarthy

J.J. McCarthy has given the Giants a reason to feel optimistic about their quarterback situation. He's thrown for at least 240 yards in each of his first two appearances and posted a passer rating of at least 90.0 in both games. That's enough production to demand Philadelphia's attention. The challenge for Vic Fangio is making sure McCarthy doesn't become comfortable.

New York's QB1 of the moment has shown that he can use his arm talent and mobility to create opportunities, but the Eagles need to make him process the game under pressure. Changing coverages, disguising pressure, and forcing him to work through progressions could disrupt the rhythm he's begun to establish.

Fangio doesn't necessarily need to blitz relentlessly to accomplish that (and he probably won't). He needs to make McCarthy uncomfortable, take away his preferred options, and force him to prove he can consistently beat a defense that knows where the pressure is coming from. Allowing him to settle into another productive afternoon would be a costly mistake.

Sean Mannion can't put Joe Milton in position to be overwhelmed by the Giants' blitz

The Giants have been aggressive defensively, with a blitz rate at 40.3% so far this season. That creates an obvious challenge for Joe Milton, particularly considering Philadelphia's problems protecting its quarterbacks. Per NBC Sports' Dave Zangaro , the Eagles have faced 109 blitzes this season and have surrendered 66 pressures, a 60.6% pressure rate that ranks worst in the league.

But there's another side to that equation. Milton has the arm strength to attack the space created when defenders vacate their coverage responsibilities. He also brings more mobility than Tanner McKee, which could give Philadelphia another way to punish an overly aggressive pass rush.

Dennard Wilson loves to send extra pressure. Philadelphia needs to make him pay for it rather than letting the Giants dictate the terms of the passing game. A few successful throws against the blitz could force Wilson to reconsider how aggressively he attacks.

Can the Eagles' run defense keep the Giants' rushing attack in check?

We've watched Saquon Barkley dominate the Giants before, and it may have slipped our minds that this Eagles team can allow New York to give Philadelphia some of its own medicine. The Giants could have a significant advantage if they can establish their running game, an Achilles' heel that has shown up with the Eagles' defense constantly.

Cam Skattebo is still recovering from a hamstring injury. John Harbaugh has left the door open for him to play as a game-time decision, but he hasn't practiced, which may mean Devin Singletary will carry the bulk of the workload.

Philadelphia has allowed 131.9 yards per game on the ground through eight weeks of the season, but if they can cure that and make the Giants one-dimensional, their chances of winning improve exponentially.

articles.title: Undefeated Pewaukee shuts out New Berlin Eisenhower in WIAA playoffs
articles.summary: Pewaukee remains undefeated after a dominant 35-0 playoff victory over New Berlin Eisenhower on Friday night.
articles.body:
PEWAUKEE − Pewaukee shut out New Berlin Eisenhower, 35-0, in a WIAA Division 3 quarterfinal football playoff game Friday, Nov. 6.

The top-seeded Pirates (12-0) controlled the game after a scoreless first quarter, building a 21-0 halftime lead before adding two touchdowns in the third quarter over the third-seeded Lions (8-4).

Junior quarterback Brooks Dobberstein completed 6 of 8 passes for 120 yards and two touchdowns, including a 56-yard scoring strike. Senior Aidan Weick caught three passes for 79 yards and a touchdown, and Dobberstein added a rushing touchdown.

Photos from Pewaukee's shut out against New Berlin Eisenhower

Junior Benji Weis led the Pirates on the ground with 166 yards and two touchdowns on 15 carries. Weis went down with an injury near halftime but walked off under his own power. He played most of the second half and scored a 50-yard rushing touchdown to start running clock, making it 35-0.

Pewaukee junior running back Colton Wall was injured in the second quarter and had to be helped off the field.

The Pirates, who also beat Eisenhower 41-8 during the regular season, will face Catholic Memorial at Wauwatosa West on Nov. 13 in the state semifinals.

articles.title: Ricky Stenhouse Jr. Says a Cup Team Needs Up to $10M in Sponsors Just to Break Even
articles.summary: Ricky Stenhouse Jr. says a Cup team needs up to $300,000 in sponsorship per race and up to $10 million a season just to break even.
articles.body:
Ricky Stenhouse Jr. says the money behind a NASCAR Cup Series car adds up fast, with up to $10 million in sponsorship needed just to break even.

On the Bring The Juice podcast , Stenhouse estimated that a team needs $250,000 to $300,000 in sponsorship for every race. Over a full season, he put the figure at $8 million to $10 million just to break even.

"You want to be a millionaire in racing and you better start with a billion," Stenhouse said.

Stenhouse also explained how race money reaches him. Race winnings come from NASCAR, and charter payments are another part of the picture.

He said his contract groups those earnings together. His share then depends on where he finishes.

"If we win I get 50%," Stenhouse said. For finishes further back, he said, "here on back is 20." He said bonuses can also come for wins and other results.

Stenhouse drives the No. 47 Chevrolet for Hyak Motorsports . He has been in the car since 2020, when the team was still JTG Daugherty Racing.

Gordon Smith later rebranded the team as Hyak. It is a single-car operation, and in May it signed Stenhouse to a multiyear extension .

"It's never easy being a single-car team," Stenhouse said at the time. He also said the team's growing experience is helping it improve.

Stenhouse has four career Cup wins. Two came with this team: the 2023 Daytona 500 and the fall 2024 race at Talladega Superspeedway.

He moved up to Cup full time in 2013 after winning back-to-back titles in what is now the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series. He was the Cup rookie of the year that season.

Others in motorsports have shared their own figures, and EssentiallySports pointed to several of them alongside Stenhouse's comments.

In previously reported comments on the Joe Vulpis podcast, Frankie Muniz estimated that a full Cup program costs $20 million to $30 million a year. He put a Truck Series program at $3 million to $7 million.

Muniz was talking about total budgets. Stenhouse's $8 million to $10 million figure was about the sponsorship needed to break even.

Kelley Earnhardt Miller has said JR Motorsports runs on a margin of about 1.5%. She said on the Business of Motorsports podcast that the team is happy to break even or make a small profit.

Alpha Prime Racing co-owner Tommy Joe Martins has said sponsorship covers at least 40% of his O'Reilly Series team's budget, and closer to 60% under its current model. He put that budget at about $2.5 million to $3 million a year.

Sponsors are a big part of silly season, too. RFK Racing is reportedly set to lose a major sponsor after this season.

Stenhouse and the No. 47 team close out their season Sunday at Homestead-Miami Speedway.

articles.title: Detroit Lions Fans Can Win Ultimate Thanksgiving Experience While Honoring Jack Campbell
articles.summary: Detroit Lions fans can bid on VIP Thanksgiving tickets and sideline passes while supporting veterans through a special auction honoring Jack Campbell.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions fans have an opportunity to enjoy an unforgettable Thanksgiving experience at Ford Field while supporting a cause close to the heart of linebacker Jack Campbell .

In honor of Veterans Day and the NFL's Salute to Service initiative, Lions fan Clemmie ( @LadyClemmieUDL ) has organized a special Thanksgiving auction , with all proceeds benefiting the Stronger Warrior Foundation in Campbell's honor.

The auction features two premium tickets to Detroit's Thanksgiving Day matchup against the Chicago Bears, along with exclusive pregame sideline access donated by the Lions.

What's Included in the Detroit Lions Thanksgiving Auction?

The winning bidder will receive an impressive Thanksgiving package for two, including:

Two pregame sideline passes , generously donated by the Detroit Lions, allowing fans to watch players warm up from just feet away.

Two premium Delta Club tickets in Section 203C for the Lions' Thanksgiving game against the Chicago Bears on November 26.

Covered game-day parking at Comerica Garage.

The sideline experience typically begins when stadium gates open and concludes approximately 30 minutes before kickoff.

The premium seats are located in an ADA-accessible row, although the winning bidder does not need to have a disability to use them.

The Lions will host the Bears at Ford Field on Thanksgiving Day, with kickoff scheduled for 1 p.m. ET.

Honoring Jack Campbell by Helping Veterans

What makes this auction particularly meaningful is its connection to Campbell.

According to Clemmie, Campbell regularly volunteered with the Stronger Warrior Foundation's Adaptive Warrior initiative, helping renovate homes for local veterans.

The Stronger Warrior Foundation's Adaptive Warrior program helps veterans with disabilities receive necessary modifications to their homes and vehicles, providing greater independence and improving their quality of life.

Following Campbell's frightening injury against the Minnesota Vikings, the Detroit community has rallied around the linebacker.

As we previously reported, Campbell recently shared an encouraging update about his recovery , thanking everyone for their overwhelming support.

Meanwhile, head coach Dan Campbell has emphasized the importance of honoring Jack while continuing to support him through his recovery.

Now, Lions fans have another opportunity to show their appreciation for Campbell by supporting a cause that has meant so much to him.

How to Bid on the Thanksgiving Experience

Bidding officially opens Saturday, November 7, at 10 a.m. ET and closes Thursday, November 12, at 9 p.m. ET.

Fans interested in participating can place their bids here .

All proceeds from the auction will be donated to the Stronger Warrior Foundation.

Whether fans bid on the experience or simply share the fundraiser, it's an opportunity to support veterans while recognizing Campbell's commitment to giving back to the community.

And for one lucky Lions fan and a guest, Thanksgiving at Ford Field could become an experience they'll never forget.

articles.title: NFL predictions: Lions vs Dolphins odds, props as Miami looks to bounce back
articles.summary: Taking a look at the latest odds and prop bets for Sunday’s Week 9 Detroit Lions vs. Miami Dolphins game.
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins lost to the New England Patriots in Week 8 and face a tough test in Week 9 as they try to bounce back against the Detroit Lions. This season, the Dolphins are focused on improving week to week and laying the foundation for future success. While they sit at 1-6 for the year, they fight each and every week, playing hard until the final whistle, a great sign for a team with 14 rookies and in the midst of a complete franchise rebuild.

The Lions come into Sunday's Week 9 game with a 5-2 record and looking like a team that can make a deep run in the NFC playoffs. After a disappointing 9-8 record in 2025 leading to a fourth-place finish in the NFC North, Detroit is looking to return to the form that brought them back-to-back division titles in 2023 and 2024. The NFC North is a tough division, however, with all four teams above the .500 mark and having won at least five times already this season.

How will Sunday's game play out? This feels like a game that could get away from the Dolphins, a byproduct of how diametrically opposed their 2026 trajectories are. The oddsmakers at FanDuel Sportsbook , however, seem to think this game might be a little tighter than might be expected.

Phins up! Dive into game day on the SB Nation app!

Celebrate every score and talk through every twist and turn with fellow Dolphins fans in real time.

Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android .

Over the last two weeks, I was right on my prediction of the Dolphins beating the Jets straight-up, and on Miami losing to New England but covering the spread. This week, I am not as bullish on the Dolphins' chances. The Lions are the better team in this matchup, and I think they'll cover the 6.5-point spread, even with the injuries they are facing. Miami will play the Lions tough, and they might keep it close for much of the game, but in the end, I think the Lions pull away.

Any time touchdown scorer: Ollie Gordon II

The Dolphins running game ran into a speedbump against the Patriots. After averaging 125 yards rushing in their last five games, Miami was held to just 74 yards in Week 8. They have to correct that in Week 9. It will not be easy, Detroit has the ninth-ranked rush defense in the league, allowing just 96.6 yards per game. The Dolphins will have to be deliberate in getting the ball to Gordon, continue to feed him even if they are getting stuffed early, and make this a physical game. In the end, I think Gordon will be able to find the endzone at least once in this game and this prop hits.

Miami has struggled covering tight ends this season, and they face another who could cause problems in LaPorta. They have allowed four tight ends to surpass the 48.5 yards mark (T.J. Hockenson, 119 yards; George Kittle, 80 yards; Mason Taylor, 62 yards; Travis Kelce, 59 yards) and would have had five on that list if Hunter Henry had not been injured in the second quarter Patriots game (3 receptions, 30 yards when he departed). Unless Miami comes with a different scheme to handle tight ends, LaPorta reaching 49 yards receiving seems likely.

Bell is averaging 12.3 yards per catch, but the rookie has not been the primary target in the passing game – where Malik Washington has nearly double the amount of targets, almost three-times the receptions, and more than double the yards. Bell has been targeted more than fellow rookie Caleb Douglas – in part because Douglas missed three games with an injury – but Douglas has one more reception and almost 80 more yards than Bell. Miami is playing it smart with Bell, who tore his ACL less than a year ago, but it has depressed some of his stats this season. The flashes are there, and Miami will need him to flash in this game if they are going to pull off the upset. His longest reception this season was for a 44-yard gain, so the potential for a big play is there. He may not pick up that big of a gain in this game, but a 14-yard reception does not seem out of reach.

articles.title: Kyren Wilson beats John Higgins to win International Championship
articles.summary: Kyren Wilson claims the 12th ranking title of his career by beating John Higgins 10-8 in the International Championship final in China.
articles.body:
Kyren Wilson claimed the 12th ranking title of his career by beating John Higgins 10-8 in a hard-fought International Championship final in China.

The 51-year-old Higgins, who was aiming to become snooker's oldest ranking event winner, took a 2-1 lead with a 141 break in the third frame.

Wilson, coming off winning the Northern Ireland Open two weeks ago, knocked in a 94 as he moved 4-3 up but four-time world champion Higgins made runs of 71 and 75 to lead 5-4 after the afternoon session.

The pair shared the opening four frames of the evening session before Wilson took three frames in a row with breaks of 80, 52 and 101 to take a 9-7 lead.

Higgins, who was beaten by world champion Wu Yize in last year's final, reduced the deficit to 9-8 but a 61 from 2024 world champion Wilson in the 18th frame gave him victory.

"It was about sticking in there and bouncing back if I made mistakes," said Wilson, who becomes the 16th player to win back-to-back ranking events.

"[Higgins] has made a career out of unbelievable clearances under pressure and has been an idol of mine since I started watching the game.

"To play him in a final like this is a dream come true and it is an honour to win."

articles.title: WWE Crown Jewel 2026 Winners, Live Grades, Reaction and Highlights
articles.summary: From the ANB Arena in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, Crown Jewel 2026 promised to decide the true top champions of WWE and put an end to a long-time rivalry.
articles.body:
Crown Jewel 2026 promised to determine WWE's top champions and settle a longstanding rivalry at the ANB Arena in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

Could Sami Zayn upset Roman Reigns? Would Chelsea Green prove she could compete at Liv Morgan's level? How would the rivalry between Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton end in their Last Man Standing match?

Check out the live grades and highlights for WWE's latest premium live event.

Last Man Standing: Cody Rhodes vs. Randy Orton

Last Time in Action: Cody Rhodes defeated Baron Corbin by disqualification (SmackDown, October 16); Randy Orton alongside Rey Fénix lost to Trick Williams in a Money in the Bank qualifier (SmackDown, September 18).

This fight quickly spilled outside into the crowd then to the stage where Orton sent Rhodes through a table for the first long count.

The two went back and forth for a while until The Viper countered the Bionic Elbow into an RKO for another near-10 count.

The American Nightmare tried to send The Viper through the announce table with a Diving Elbow off a ladder, but Orton ducked it, nearly winning the match.

Orton went for the Punt, but Rhodes ducked it, hitting a Cody Cutter and Cross Rhodes for nine. The American Nightmare threatened to blast The Viper with a steel chair on the steps, but Orton caught him with a Low Blow.

Rhodes caught The Viper with a trifecta of Cross Rhodes, cutting open Orton with the steel steps on the last impact. The American Nightmare stopped referee Charles Robinson's count to hit Orton with a Punt to win.

For the final stage of a personal rivalry, this was a flat performance from both men. While Orton typically works at this methodical pace, Rhodes did nothing to speed it up.

This did little to engage an audience that was surprisingly flat for a battle of two top WWE stars, even throwing "You suck!" chants at Rhodes.

Compared to their WrestleMania 42 match, this had less intensity beyond a possibly inadvertent head shot into the steel steps late.

If this had led to an American Nightmare turn, it would have been better received, but it left Rhodes in the cliché regretful face spot after choosing to Punt Orton.

Once an exciting possibility, the Rhodes vs. Orton feud ends with a whimper, leaving the question of why WWE spent three years building this as a major rivalry.

The crowd did not get the memo that Orton was the heel in this match, cheering him more than Rhodes throughout.

Rhodes delivered an Orton-like Draping DDT to the delight of Corey Graves who threw a "Vintage Rhodes" at Michael Cole.

The fastest Orton moved all match was when he had to sell a dramatic near-10 count.

Afterward, Rhodes sat on the apron, selling that he regretted what he did to Orton.

World Tag Championships: Bron Breakker & Austin Theory (w/ Maxxine Dupri) vs. Penta & Je'Von Evans

Last Time in Action: Austin Theory and Bron Breakker alongside Bronson Reed defeated Penta and Je'Von Evans alongside Dragon Lee (Raw, October 2).

After a hot start, The Vision isolated Penta for a while. When Je'Von Evans got the hot tag, he started to push the pace.

The Vision struggled to contain the athletic challengers, who almost picked up the win off a Frog Splash.

Maxxine Dupri saved Theory from the near-fall, then Bronson Reed arrived to take out Penta and Evans to turn the tide.

This brought out Oba Femi, who tossed Auszilla through a table off the stage. Penta took out Breakker on the floor, then the luchador and Evans finished Theory with a Mexican Destroyer–OG Cutter combination.

This was one of the best tag team matches WWE has put on all year. The action was fast and dynamic, and the crowd was loud and engaged.

The twists and turns followed the story The Vision had set up over the past year, finally delivering an emphatic answer to the stable's numbers advantage.

All four men were great throughout, though The Young OG especially drove the crowd into a frenzy when he was fighting back.

Oba's arrival was the emotional climax of the contest and made the most of The Ruler as the top babyface on Raw right now.

While Penta and Evans are not an established tag team, they looked great together and showed why they can carry a struggling division forward.

These two should defend the titles regularly on TV against the underused stars of Raw, and it will become appointment television.

Evans and Penta def. Breakker and Theory by pinfall to become the new world tag team champions.

The crowd was hotter for Penta in The Vision's beatdown segment than anything from the opener.

The Young OG ran to the corner at one point to tag in Penta, not realizing he was down on the floor, leading to a funny turnaround into both champs.

The Ruler held up the hands of the new tag team champions on the stage, selling this as a unified force against The Vision. Give them a stable name!

Women's Crown Jewel Championship: Liv Morgan vs. Chelsea Green

Last Time in Action: Liv Morgan alongside Raquel Rodriguez and Roxanne Perez defeated Chelsea Green alongside Tiffany Stratton and Iyo Sky (Raw, November 2).

Liv taunted Green from the opening bell, causing her to doubt herself. Even after a strong slap from the WWE women's champion to the Women's world champion, Liv kept control.

Green's second slap to Liv on the top rope turned the tide, followed by a Superplex. Liv teased an Unpretty-Her on Green, but the WWE women's champion countered into a Rough Ryder near-fall.

After a pair of Topes to the floor, Green countered an ObLivion into an Unpretty-Her, but Liv got her foot on the bottom rope.

Raquel and Roxanne arrived to help Liv, but the Women's world champion promised she could win alone. Liv went for another ObLivion, but Green grabbed the ropes then stacked up Liv for the three count.

Afterward, Triple H came out to give Green the Crown Jewel Championship. Green talked up finally proving herself, but Liv attacked.

Stratton arrived to cash in. Green helped take out The Judgment Day, only for Stratton to blast her with the briefcase and cash in on her friend. Tiffy pinned Green after the Prettiest Moonsault.

Liv and Green do not have much chemistry, but they told a strong consistent story throughout this contest.

Liv played the annoying confident heel well, goading Green into fully believing in herself down the stretch. It is a shame though that the actual win was just a basic win, not more definitive.

The aftermath was the expected payoff after weeks of repeating the same cash-in set-up every week. Stratton was always going to turn on Green, not take down Liv.

That said, the actual execution did not make sense for the story to this point. Why have The Judgment Day not play a factor in Stratton's decision to take out Green instead of Liv?

The way this played out, it hardly even mattered that Liv was there at all, which undermines the entire point of this specific build-up.

Still, WWE should have a strong storyline for SmackDown's women's division going forward after this cash-in.

Stratton vs. Green is immediately the hottest angle in the women's division, which was desperately needed.

Green def. Morgan by pinfall to become the 2026 women's Crown Jewel champion; Stratton def. Green by pinfall to become the new WWE women's champion.

One enthused fan screamed out "I love you, Liv Morgan!" multiple times.

The cameras caught some great shots early juxtaposing Liv's cockiness and Green's struggles to sell the story.

Corey Graves multiple times countered the obvious story playing out in the ring by trying to sell Green's demeanor as inconsistent.

Green plays the sympathetic babyface well but needs to work on her strikes to make her comebacks look more fluid.

Men's Crown Jewel Championship: Roman Reigns vs. Sami Zayn

Last Time in Action: Sami Zayn defeated Trick Williams to retain the Undisputed WWE Championship (SmackDown, October 30); Roman Reigns defeated LA Knight to retain the World Heavyweight Championship (Money in the Bank, October 10).

Zayn carried the crowd reaction early, fighting with explosive power. Reigns wore him down with strong offense, but The Last Real Good Guy would not stay down.

Zayn ducked a Superman Punch into a Blue Thunder Bomb for a near-fall. Zayn went for the Helluva Kick, but Reigns ducked it and landed a Superman Punch for a near-fall.

The OTC avoided another Helluva Kick then landed a second Superman Punch. When Reigns called for the Spear though, The Last Real Good Guy finally caught him with the Helluva Kick for a close near-fall.

Zayn teased a Superman Punch. Reigns avoided it then accidentally caught the referee Chad Patton with a Superman Punch.

Zayn caught Reigns with an Exploder into a second Helluva Kick. Charles Robinson ran down to finally count, and Reigns kicked out.

Zayn took out Robinson in anger with a Helluva Kick then grabbed the WWE Championship. The OTC ducked it and hit the Rebound Spear, but a slow count from a recovering Patton allowed Zayn to kick out.

The two champions exchanged strikes that left Reigns standing tall. He hit a Superman Punch. Zayn countered a second into an Exploder but then ran into a Superman Punch.

Zayn responded with his own Superman Punch, but when The Last Real Good Guy teased his own Spear, he ran into a Spear from Reigns. Another Rebound Spear finally kept Zayn down.

Afterward, The Last Real Good Guy demanded a handshake, but Reigns gave him a family hug instead and called him an Uso.

The OTC then ended the show by calling for the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to acknowledge him.

A match like this was always going to go a bit over-the-top, verging on indulgent, but Reigns and Zayn have so much chemistry that it worked.

Much like the Knight match at MITB, Reigns faced a game competitor that gained his respect, even if they could not quite keep The OTC down.

While he fell short, Zayn looked better against Reigns than he has against any recent opponents. He did not need shortcuts to almost take down The OTC.

Arguably, The Last Real Good Guy got much more out of this than The OTC did. The win just further sells that WWE will not let Reigns lose any steam until he collides with Oba Femi.

Reigns and Zayn seemingly reconciling could lead to The Last Real Good Guy helping The Bloodline in the fight against The 946, but it is not directly necessary since Zayn has enough going on on SmackDown as it is.

Hopefully, WWE does not go right back to having Zayn rely on shortcuts to retain his title after he showed he could hold his own against Reigns.

Reigns def. Zayn by pinfall to become the 2026 men's Crown Jewel champion.

Saudi Arabia remains a rare pro-Zayn crowd during his heel run.

Zayn was immediately disrespectful to Reigns, gloating in his face during the introductions and throwing his jacket at The OTC.

After the Rebound Spear kick-out, Reigns told Zayn he respected his fight but promised to finish him off.

Triple H once again appeared afterward to give over the Crown Jewel Championship, though it did not lead to a MITB cash-in.

Crown Jewel did not look like a good show on paper. The Crown Jewel Championship still does not matter to WWE as a whole, and the tag title match came off as filler.

The talent absolutely over-delivered on the potential of this card, particularly the World Tag Team Championships and men's Crown Jewel Championship matches.

Even Chelsea Green vs. Liv Morgan, despite some awkward booking, played out better than expected.

The only downer was the lackluster Cody Rhodes vs. Randy Orton, but at least this should be the end of a rivalry that has mostly held SmackDown back in 2026.

Beyond the tag title win and Money in the Bank cash-in, not much is likely to come from this show long term, but it was one of WWE's more complete nights of pure action in 2026.

articles.title: Cody Rhodes vs. Randy Orton Last Man Standing Winner, Top Highlights from WWE Crown Jewel 2026
articles.summary: Cody Rhodes beat Randy Orton in a Last Man Standing match at WWE Crown Jewel on Saturday.
articles.body:
Cody Rhodes beat Randy Orton in a Last Man Standing match at WWE Crown Jewel on Saturday.

In a brutally physical bout, Rhodes finally put Orton down for a 10-count by hitting him with The Viper's own signature punt:

Real Winners and Losers of Crown Jewel ⬆️⬇️

Rhodes absorbed a ton of punishment en route to victory, including going through a folding table and the announce table and taking a low blow:

The rivalry between Rhodes and Orton dates back to before WrestleMania 42 when Orton turned heel by viciously attacking his longtime friend ahead of their Undisputed WWE Championship match.

Rhodes beat Orton at WrestleMania to retain the WWE title, but The Viper got the last laugh in many respects by laying The American Nightmare out with a punt after the match.

Orton disappeared from WWE programming for the next few months, but he resurfaced at SummerSlam to cost Rhodes in his Undisputed WWE Championship match against CM Punk.

A month later, Orton and Rhodes clashed in a grudge match at Sunday Night's Main Event, and Cody appeared to have Randy right where he wanted him.

The American Nightmare hesitated while preparing for a punt, though, allowing Orton to hit him with a low blow and RKO for the victory.

With their rivalry becoming increasingly personal each week, Rhodes and Orton got into a number of physical and verbal skirmishes on SmackDown.

Rhodes eventually took it out on Baron Corbin by hitting him with a punt following a match that ended in a disqualification thanks to interference by Orton.

With that, Rhodes made it clear that he had the killer instinct needed to go up against and potentially beat Orton.

Orton accepted Cody's proposal of a Last Man Standing match at Crown Jewel, and although Randy did not seem to believe that Rhodes had what it took to beat him in such a brutal environment, The American Nightmare proved him wrong at Crown Jewel.

articles.title: Penta & Je'Von Evans Beat The Vision to Win World Tag Titles at WWE Crown Jewel as Oba Femi Returns
articles.summary: Penta and Je'Von Evans beat The Vision's Bron Breakker and Austin Theory at WWE Crown Jewel on Saturday to win the World Tag Team Championships.
articles.body:
Penta and Je'Von Evans beat The Vision's Bron Breakker and Austin Theory at WWE Crown Jewel on Saturday to win the World Tag Team Championships.

Bronson Reed interfered in an effort to help Breakker and Theory retain, but Oba Femi returned after several weeks away to even the odds:

Real Winners and Losers of Crown Jewel ⬆️⬇️

With Reed taken out and Breakker distracted by Femi, Penta and Evans hit Theory with a Mexican Destroyer followed by an OG Cutter to win the titles:

Saturday's bout was a long time coming since Penta and Evans have been at odds with The Vision dating back to September.

After Evans won a Triple Threat match that included Theory to qualify for the men's Money in the Bank ladder match on the Sept. 14 episode of Raw, Evans faced Breakker in a singles match one week later.

The bout ended in a disqualification when Theory interfered and The Vision launched an attack against The Young OG.

Over the next two weeks, Evans and Penta teamed up successfully on two occasions, beating The Judgment Day's Dominik Mysterio and JD McDonagh, as well as Breakker and Theory in a non-title match.

Just days after Penta and Evans beat Breakker and Theory, three of them competed in the men's Money in the Bank ladder match.

Penta won the bout, while Breakker tossed Evans from the top of a ladder and through the roof of an ambulance.

Despite the scary fall, Evans returned one week later on Raw and helped Penta beat Breakker in a singles match by foiling Theory's interference attempt.

On the Oct. 26 edition of Raw, The Vision brutally attacked Evans after he lost a WWE Championship match against Sami Zayn. Penta made the save, but he got beaten down at the hands of The Vision as well.

Penta and Evans then appealed to Raw general manager Adam Pearce for a World Tag Team Championship opportunity, and Pearce granted it.

Penta and Evans made The Vision pay for their recent attacks by winning their first tag team titles in WWE.

articles.title: Nueva versión sobre la ausencia de Jorge Carrascal en la Selección Colombia: destapan los verdaderos motivos
articles.standfirst: El jugador no fue incluido en la última lista de Néstor Lorenzo
articles.summary: El jugador no fue incluido en la última lista de Néstor Lorenzo
articles.body: La ausencia de Jorge Carrascal de la Selección Colombia para los amistosos de noviembre ante Chile ha generado dos relatos contrapuestos: uno apunta a un conflicto con el técnico Néstor Lorenzo y otro, surgido en Brasil, sostiene que el propio jugador pidió quedarse para priorizar la recta final del Brasileirão con Flamengo. Por ahora, ninguna de las dos versiones cuenta con confirmación oficial completa. Jorge Carrascal no apareció en la lista de 26 convocados por Néstor Lorenzo para los amistosos contra Chile, programados para el 13 y el 17 de noviembre. La exclusión llamó la atención porque el cartagenero atraviesa un buen momento con Flamengo: había sumado 27 partidos, siete goles y nueve asistencias en la temporada, cifras que lo posicionaban como un candidato razonable para volver al equipo nacional. La sorpresa fue mayor porque, antes de conocerse la nómina, varios medios daban por hecho que Carrascal sería tenido en cuenta. Su rendimiento ofensivo, su regularidad en un Flamengo que pelea el título del Brasileirão y su perfil de mediocampista creativo hacían que su nombre fuera uno de los más esperados en la convocatoria. La primera explicación que tomó fuerza en Colombia provino del periodista Felipe Sierra, quien afirmó que Carrascal no quería volver a la Selección mientras Néstor Lorenzo siguiera como entrenador. Según esa versión, existía una relación deteriorada entre ambos tras desacuerdos durante el Mundial 2026. Sierra sostuvo que Carrascal se habría sentido traicionado por no haber jugado ni un minuto en el Mundial, pese a haber defendido públicamente al técnico. También aseguró que, después del partido ante Ghana, el jugador habría criticado a Lorenzo en una conversación privada y que el entrenador habría quedado molesto con él y con otro futbolista aún no identificado. Esta versión explica la ausencia como una crisis de confianza: Carrascal no querría ser convocado mientras permanezca Lorenzo, y el cuerpo técnico tampoco tendría interés inmediato en reintegrarlo. Sin embargo, es una información de fuente periodística, no una declaración oficial del jugador, de la Federación Colombiana de Fútbol ni del cuerpo técnico. En las últimas horas ha salido una explicación distinta publicada por Coluna do Fla, medio vinculado a Flamengo. Según el reportero Rock Hudson, Carrascal habría pedido su liberación de la Selección Colombia para esta fecha FIFA, con el objetivo de concentrarse en los entrenamientos y no alejarse de Flamengo en la parte decisiva del Brasileirão. Bajo esa lectura, la ausencia no respondería a un enfrentamiento personal con Lorenzo, sino a una decisión deportiva y profesional: Carrascal habría preferido permanecer en Río de Janeiro, descansar y prepararse para los cuatro partidos finales que Flamengo tiene para definir el título local. El medio brasileño incluso interpretó esa supuesta petición como una muestra de compromiso del colombiano con la campaña del club. Esta versión encaja con el contexto deportivo: Flamengo lidera la tabla y tenía serias opciones de campeonar, mientras que Carrascal venía de salir del partido contra Grêmio con molestias musculares. El técnico Leonardo Jardim había advertido públicamente que el club necesitaba manejar con cuidado la carga de sus jugadores internacionales en el cierre de temporada. Explicó que Carrascal tenía una sobrecarga en el aductor y que fue sustituido al descanso del partido ante Grêmio por dolor muscular, aunque aclaró que no se trataba de una lesión. Jardim también señaló que Flamengo conversaba con los cuerpos técnicos de las selecciones de sus jugadores para cuidar su condición física. Sus declaraciones —“es el final de la temporada, tenemos que ser aún más cuidadosos que en los anteriores parones”— fueron interpretadas como una solicitud para no exigir de más a Carrascal durante la fecha FIFA. Aquí aparece el principal problema informativo: la versión brasileña de que Carrascal pidió no ser convocado choca directamente con la información de Marcello Neves, periodista de Globo Esporte, recogida por Caracol. Según Neves, Flamengo no habría pedido que el jugador quedara fuera y Carrascal tampoco habría solicitado quedarse en Brasil durante la fecha FIFA. Para Neves, la decisión fue exclusivamente deportiva de Néstor Lorenzo, quien definió la lista de 26 jugadores sin incluir al mediocampista. Es decir, una fuente brasileña afirma que hubo una petición de liberación, mientras otra fuente brasileña de mayor alcance afirma que no la hubo y que la exclusión fue una elección del seleccionador.

articles.title: Tiffany Stratton Wins WWE Women's Title After Chelsea Green Beats Liv Morgan at Crown Jewel 2026
articles.summary: WWE women's champion Chelsea Green won the Women's Crown Jewel Championship on Saturday, as she defeated women's world champion Liv Morgan at the Crown Jewel premium live event.
articles.body:
WWE women's champion Chelsea Green won the Women's Crown Jewel Championship on Saturday, as she defeated women's world champion Liv Morgan at the Crown Jewel premium live event.

However, Tiffany Stratton surprisingly took advantage of her friend after the match by cashing in her Money in the Bank contract to beat Green for the WWE Women's Championship.

Green beat Morgan with a roll-up after avoiding her Oblivion finisher, leading to a raucous celebration, much to the delight of the Saudi Arabian crowd:

Predicting Next Year's Crown Jewel Matches 🔮

While cutting an emotional promo about her victory, Green was attacked from behind by Morgan, and Stratton ran out in an apparent effort to make the save.

Stratton's apparent rescue was a ruse, though, as she hit Green in the face with the Money in the Bank briefcase and pinned her to become champion.

Morgan vs. Green came into focus in recent months, as Green won a ladder match for the vacant WWE Women's Championship at SummerSlam in August, while Morgan won a Triple Threat match against Stephanie Vaquer and Becky Lynch at Money in the Bank in October to become women's world champ.

Both Morgan and Green faced some tough obstacles en route to Crown Jewel, though, as they were tasked with putting their titles on the line.

On the Oct. 26 episode of Raw, Morgan unexpectedly had to defend the Women's World Championship when Vaquer was not medically cleared to compete in a No. 1 Contender's match against Lynch.

Lynch was given a title shot as a result, and she seemed to have Morgan beaten until The Judgment Day interfered by attacking her, thus causing the disqualification.

Both Green and Iyo Sky ran down to save The Man from further damage, and Stratton nearly cashed in her Money in the Bank contract on Liv before Dominik Mysterio pulled her out of the ring.

Days later on SmackDown, Green had a title defense against Nikki Bella, and it was a successful one, as Chelsea rolled up Nikki for the win.

Morgan confronted Green after the match, and while Liv was distracted by Stratton making her entrance, Chelsea laid her out with the Unpretty-Her.

Stratton tried to cash in on Morgan again, only for The Judgment Day's Roxanne Perez and Raquel Rodriguez to prevent it.

There was no shortage of tension between Morgan and Green entering Saturday's match, and while Chelsea got some retribution, it was Stratton who got the last laugh.

articles.title: Randy Orton, Sami Zayn, Real Winners and Losers of WWE Crown Jewel Match Card
articles.summary: The lead-up to this year's Crown Jewel PLE was full of unknowns and speculation, but the event has come and gone without an issue.
articles.body:
The lead-up to this year's Crown Jewel PLE was full of unknowns and speculation, but the event has come and gone without an issue.

For the third year in a row, the company had its world and WWE champions in both the men's and women's divisions fight for the Crown Jewel titles.

In addition to those bouts, we also saw Cody Rhodes battle Randy Orton in a Last Man Standing match, and Penta and Je'Von Evans challenged The Vision for the tag titles.

Let's take a look at who the real winners and losers were from Saturday's Crown Jewel event.

WWE sent a smaller crew to Saudi Arabia this year, which meant the announcers were not calling the show live from the arena.

Instead, Michael Cole and Corey Graves called the show remotely from the United States.

While that meant missing out on the atmosphere of the live crowd in Riyadh, it also spared them the long flights and other demands of international travel.

Both Winners and Losers: Randy Orton and Cody Rhodes

Orton and Rhodes were in the opening slot with their Last Man Standing match. The fans in the arena were hyped and chanted for The Viper despite him being the clear villain in this story.

CM Punk and Kevin Owens had a chaotic no-disqualification match on Friday's SmackDown, leaving Orton and Rhodes with a tough act to follow less than 24 hours later.

They fought in the crowd and used weapons just like Punk and Owens, but never quite reached the same level of intensity. Their feud is just as personal, if not more so, making the lack of animosity during the match surprising.

That said, Rhodes and Orton still put on an enjoyable show. The match followed a relatively predictable pattern, but most of what they did looked good.

The biggest difference was the pacing. Orton and Rhodes had stretches where little happened, whereas Punk and Owens barely slowed down. Without that comparison, their match might have stood out more over the weekend.

The physicality picked up as things progressed, and they were given a long time to work, so we did get to see some big spots that elevated the match. The American Nightmare scored the win with a punt kick.

We want to be clear about something: Labeling Rhodes and Orton as both winners and losers has more to do with the timing and booking of everything than their performance.

They delivered an entertaining match, but management did not do their story justice, and having to follow a great showing from Punk and Owens did them no favors.

Winners: Penta, Je'Von Evans and Oba Femi

The only scheduled match with a regularly defended championship at stake saw Austin Theory and Bron Breakker defend the World Tag Team Championships against Penta and Je'Von Evans.

Penta and Evans are not a regular team, but neither were Theory and Breakker before winning the belts, so it felt like this was a perfect illustration of how far the Raw tag team division has fallen.

However, Penta and Evans are both exciting performers, so it wasn't hard for them to put on a decent match against two guys as athletic as Theory and Breakker.

Evans and Breakker were especially entertaining, and this match helped show why they are both future main event stars just waiting for their chance to break out.

Bronson Reed showed up and interfered, but it wasn't enough to put Evans and Penta away. Oba Femi soon arrived and threw Reed off the stage through some equipment.

The distraction allowed Evans and Penta to get the victory and win the tag titles, giving the crowd a feel-good moment and Evans his first title on the main roster. Now, Penta has a tag title and the Money in the Bank briefcase.

Meanwhile, Femi looks like an absolute star in every appearance, and this one was no different. Even without a match, he ended up having one of the most memorable moments on the show.

The Vision may have lost the tag titles, but this opens up much more interesting possibilities for one member of the group.

For the past few months, Breakker has felt like the odd man out in The Vision. He never seems to match the energy of the rest of the group, and it feels like he has been ready to move on for a while.

Losing the tag titles will allow him to either leave The Vision peacefully or wipe out the entire group on his way out.

Management clearly sees him as a future top star, and getting him started on that path is best done sooner rather than later.

With the Royal Rumble just a few months away, WWE has time to build him up into a potential winner by then.

Losers: Fans in the Same Section as the Screaming Fan; Winner: Chelsea Green

Liv Morgan had a chance to win the Women's Crown Jewel Championship for the second time, but Chelsea Green was standing in her way.

The story coming into this bout was that Green was afraid that losing to Morgan would confirm that every mean thing Liv had said to her was true.

Morgan has played a great bully in this feud, and having already won the Crown Jewel title once gave her trash talk some credibility.

During the match, one fan in particular could be heard screaming at the top of their lungs for Morgan. Whoever was seated within 20 rows of that fan probably left the arena with ringing in their ears.

After a competitive back-and-forth match, Green was able to secure the victory and win the Crown Jewel Championship. She looked extremely happy and celebrated with everyone around the ring before she was presented with the massive title belt.

Loser: Chelsea Green; Winner: Tiffany Stratton

As Green was delivering a promo to celebrate her win, Morgan attacked her from behind. Tiffany Stratton showed up and took out Morgan with her briefcase before telling the ref she wanted to cash in.

Green helped fend off Raquel Rodriguez and Roxanne Perez, but then Tiffy turned on her and nailed her with the briefcase before telling the ref she was cashing in on Green, not Morgan.

She hit her moonsault and won the WWE Women's Championship, but she also took the Crown Jewel title belt and ring with her.

Stratton returning to being a heel feels like a good decision, but having it happen at the expense of Green's WWE Women's Championship reign. She was just starting to gain some momentum, and now it's over.

The final match on the card saw Roman Reigns and Sami Zayn fight over the men's Crown Jewel Championship.

This was another chapter in a story that WWE has been telling for years. Zayn's relationship with The Bloodline has had its ups and downs, and right now is definitely a down period.

This bout unfolded the same way most of Reigns' matches tend to go. It had a slow, steady pace with bursts of quick offense from both men. They did a lot of selling and tried to make it as dramatic as possible.

Reigns is at the stage in his career where he has done just about everything there is to do, so Zayn came into this bout with so much more to gain.

If The OTC won, this would just be another victory in a long string of forgettable wins. But if Zayn were victorious, he would overcome one of the biggest challenges he has faced in his career.

Unfortunately, WWE went with the safe and predictable option by having Reigns get the win. The show ended with Zayn leaving as The Tribal Chief celebrated a win nobody will remember in six months.

World heavyweight champion Roman Reigns beat undisputed WWE champion Sami Zayn at Crown Jewel on Saturday to win the Men's Crown Jewel Championship.

Reigns kicked out of a Helluva Kick, then survived another after an incapacitated referee delayed the count until a replacement arrived. Zayn later survived a spear following another delayed count.

Reigns' Crown Jewel Win Sets Up a Huge L Soon 😈

Ultimately, Reigns hit Zayn with a pair of spears to win the match, and they showed their respect for one another afterward with a hug:

This year marked the third time that the top champions in WWE's men's and women's divisions clashed at Crown Jewel for the right to be recognized as Crown Jewel champion, and the battle for the men's title featured two Superstars with a significant amount of history.

In 2022, Zayn began working with Reigns and The Bloodline. Although some members of the group were resistant to Zayn's involvement, he was eventually named Honorary Uce and became a key part of the stable.

Zayn helped Reigns in his matches on numerous occasions, and he is a big reason why The Tribal Chief was world champion for 1,316 consecutive days.

Things broke down between Zayn and Reigns at Royal Rumble 2023, though, when Sami refused to join The Bloodline in brutally attacking his longtime friend, Kevin Owens.

Zayn hit Reigns with a steel chair instead, leading to a massive showdown between them at Elimination Chamber in Zayn's hometown of Montreal.

Reigns won the match and retained the title, but Zayn ultimately still got vengeance against The Bloodline by teaming with Owens to beat The Usos for the Undisputed WWE Tag Team Championships in the main event of Night 1 of WrestleMania 39.

Zayn later reunited with Reigns and The Usos as part of the Original Bloodline ahead of Survivor Series: WarGames in 2024. Their shared history returned to the forefront heading into Crown Jewel, where they entered as WWE's two men's world champions.

In the weeks leading up to Crown Jewel, Reigns and Zayn rehashed some of what happened between them in the past, and Sami took umbrage with Roman perhaps not taking him seriously as a threat.

Zayn had a chance to prove he could hang with Reigns and even beat him at Crown Jewel, but The OTC rose to the occasion as he so often does and secured the Men's Crown Jewel Championship.

articles.title: Roman Reigns' Win at WWE Crown Jewel vs. Sami Zayn Sets Him Up For a Massive L Soon
articles.summary: Roman Reigns picking up a win over Sami Zayn at Crown Jewel will surely set the pro wrestling fanbase ablaze yet again.
articles.body:
Roman Reigns picking up a win over Sami Zayn at Crown Jewel will surely set the pro wrestling fanbase ablaze yet again.

As the age-old adage in the sport goes, though, the worst reaction is no reaction. And this particular outcome with Reigns and Zayn is a measured decision that aligns with ongoing themes and sets up big surprises at landmarks like Survivor Series soon.

In fact, Reigns beating Zayn is hardly surprising. The biggest shocker of the night from Saudi Arabia was the fact that Royce Keyes' 946 didn't interfere.

Real Winners and Losers of Crown Jewel ⬆️⬇️

Talk about coming full circle: The biggest complaint about Reigns during his Bloodline days was that he always won dirty and with an assist. Now…fans are mad he's winning clean and there's little outside shenanigans.

Said fans aren't really paying attention, considering this current Reigns run has been all about him picking up clean wins. It's all for the long-term benefit of the obvious Oba Femi match at next year's WrestleMania.

It also benefits Keyes and 946. When the faction warfare unfolds at Survivor Series, there's a little leeway for Reigns to take a beating and a loss, maybe even eating a pin. That's the only time on the calendar before 'Mania that was ever realistic for Reigns to take a loss.

Cementing a new faction by having them beat down and win over the previously dominant faction is a no-brainer route. That PLE also offers layers of angles to spin off, too, since Solo Sikoa or Jacob Fatu could play a role that actually costs Reigns a win.

And to be blunt, we have to stop pretending that Zayn needed the win over Reigns, or even that the loss devalues him. His stock has never been higher in WWE. Now he's getting main-event programs with Reigns that continue a story years in the making.

Want to see devalued? Take a gander at fan favorite LA Knight, who gets chances and losses, chances and losses, while becoming a meme online when a WWE docuseries reveals that the powers behind the scenes are iffy on him right before the botch lowlight reels.

The 42-year-old Zayn will be fine. Reigns is a vehicle to put over the next generation. Scoff all you want, but his getting involved with 946 is absolutely massive for the members of that stable. A faction that is mostly 32 years old or younger.

Also in that age bracket and the "next generation of the very top of the sport" bracket? The 28-year-old Femi.

Truth might hurt, but this isn't about building up Reigns. A loss tomorrow would mint his challenger for life. It's more about common sense. There's a vocal portion of the pro wrestling fanbase sticking its collective fingers in its ears, pretending this is still Big Dog Roman Reigns when it's not. WWE can't win with how it's handling Reigns, but it's inarguable that he's the top guy with the most crossover appeal to non-wrestling sectors right now.

WWE can't really win at Survivor Series with that sort of fan, either, because Reigns losing won't be a "loss" to them. What it can do, though, is put 946 in the best position to succeed by using his star power and this general angst about all things Reigns to make them look good and keep the momentum going.

We'll revisit this sort of topic if WWE bellyflops and has Bloodline win at the next big PLE or just generally botches the whole thing. If it's all just a ruse to fulfill a PLE's namesake before nothing from before it matters again, well, that's an issue everyone hoped WWE had outgrown.

But for now? Zayn isn't worse off from the "loss" at an overseas show with a made-up title that most fans agree isn't all that important anyway. Reigns isn't "stronger" for it. He is, though, set up for a loss that could really matter to the promotion's future before the year's out, so fans would be wise to look past the initial knee-jerk reaction for now.

articles.title: Arturo Coello y Coki Nieto dan a España su quinto Mundial de pádel
articles.standfirst: Vencieron a Tino Libaak y Gonza Alfonso en el tercer partido de la final y devuelven el título a España cinco años después
articles.summary: Vencieron a Tino Libaak y Gonza Alfonso en el tercer partido de la final y devuelven el título a España cinco años después
articles.body: España vuelve a tocar el cielo del pádel mundial. El equipo masculino se ha llevado su quinto Mundial de pádel tras doblegar a Argentina en la gran final y con Arturo Coello y Coki Nieto como protagonistas tumbando a Tino Libaak y Gonza Alfonso en el tercer y definitivo punto de la final. Doha asistió, una vez más, a un espectáculo tremendo entre las dos grandes potencias de este deporte que, por tercera edición seguida, dejaron todo para el último duelo de la noche. En él, esta vez la dupla española, que ya sabía lo que era jugar en una final, se llevó el gato al agua y llevó un nuevo título a las vitrinas de la Federación Española de Pádel. Coello y Nieto, en una elección a priori sorprendente de Juanjo Gutiérrez por aquello de dejar al número 1 para el tercer partido, fueron los ejecutores definitivos ante unos Libaak y Alfonso que lo dieron absolutamente todo pero que no pudieron con una pareja que tuvo muchos menos errores y que leyó mejor el guion del partido desde el principio. Se acabaron llevando la batalla final por 6-3 y 6-2. Un título que rompe la hegemonía de Argentina, que buscaba el tercero seguido tras los de 2022 y 2024, y que devuelve la alegría al pádel masculino español con la que muchos consideran es la mejor generación de pádel de su historia hasta ahora. En el primer punto, el debutante Aimar Goñi y el Lobo, Juan Lebrón, abrocharon la primera victoria para los españoles tras una remontada espectacular ante Di Nenno y Augsburger. 5-7, 7-5 y 6-2 que hacían soñar a los de Juanjo Gutiérrez con el entorchado mundialista. Pero aún quedaba tarea por hacer. Eso sí, en el segundo asalto, un vendaval formado por Tapia y Chingotto pasó por encima de Paquito y Jon Sanz, que vieron cómo los argentinos igualaban la contienda con un indiscutible 6-1 y 6-2 que mandaba la partida al definitivo asalto. En el tercero, Coki y Arturo culminaron la semana con el ansiado título que deja de nuevo al pádel español en lo más alto.

articles.title: Clean Hit: Steelers LG Mason McCormick Not Fined for Body-Slamming Jared Verse
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers guard Mason McCormick was not fined by the NFL for slamming Cleveland Browns defensive end Jared Verse after […]
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers guard Mason McCormick was not fined by the NFL for slamming Cleveland Browns defensive end Jared Verse after an extra point attempt on Sunday.

McCormick was flagged for unnecessary roughness after Verse jumped to block the Pittsburgh extra point attempt in the second quarter of what became a 27-6 Steelers victory . Verse landed on McCormick and the Steelers guard slammed him to the turf, earning a 15-yard penalty that was enforced on the ensuing kickoff.

Mason McCormick called for a personal foul against Jared Verse on the extra point. Awfully soft. We've already heard way more than we needed to from this officiating crew. pic.twitter.com/PzcfE2p7ql — Alan Saunders (@ASaunders_PGH) November 1, 2026

Mason McCormick called for a personal foul against Jared Verse on the extra point. Awfully soft. We've already heard way more than we needed to from this officiating crew. pic.twitter.com/PzcfE2p7ql

Alan Saunders (@ASaunders_PGH) November 1, 2026

The lack of supplemental discipline suggests that the league office did not support the penalty call on review, as most personal fouls also include a fine.

Earlier this week, Browns special teams coach Byron Storer called it dirty play and uncalled for.

"It's a guy that takes his legs out and slams him to the ground. There's no way we would discuss that. That's not what we're about," Storer told Cleveland reporters on Thursday. "The NFL is, you know, we're going out there battling each other each and every week, but we're not trying to hurt anybody. To me, it's a fine line there between preventing someone to make a block and intentionally trying to hurt someone in that situation. I don't agree with the way that play went down. We have to be careful there. That play should be penalized."

#Browns ST coordinator Byron Storer condemned #Steelers G Mason McCormick body-slamming Jared Verse with intent to hurt: pic.twitter.com/HJyPLuhuCZ — Mary Kay Cabot (@MaryKayCabot) November 5, 2026

#Browns ST coordinator Byron Storer condemned #Steelers G Mason McCormick body-slamming Jared Verse with intent to hurt: pic.twitter.com/HJyPLuhuCZ

Mary Kay Cabot (@MaryKayCabot) November 5, 2026

Verse made his thoughts clear about McCormick after the loss.

"Like what I've said before about them, that's just the way that they are. Him specifically, that's the way he plays. That was just a lack of awareness on my part. I should've had a better grasp of the type of player I was going up against. That's on me," Verse said about leaping on the extra point.

Verse added: "To do something like that, I just can't have respect for that … I jumped in the air, tried to block the kick. He swept my legs in the air, ended up landing on my head. That's football. I'm very upset about it and if this wasn't football, I'd be acting a different way. He got a flag; we were able to walk away with a yellow penalty on them."

When asked if it was a dirty play, Verse said, "The refs called it how they called it. I'm not going to add any more fuel to the fire. But I thought it was a very uncalled for play."

Verse had spent the week leading up to the game calling the Steelers offensive line dirty. McCormick said he wasn't aware that it was Verse who jumped on him.

"Yeah, I really had no idea who it was. I just felt somebody jump and we're told to get jumpers hands down. And that's really it," McCormick told Brendan Howe of Steelers Now .

Verse called out his teammates for not defending him after he was slammed on his head.

"That honestly could have put me in a position to not be able to finish the season, put me in a position to change my life in a very bad aspect … the lack of reaction by those around me had upset me a lot," Verse said on Thursday.

"I made my concerns known, I've made my issues known about the situation."

The New York Jets will be without three additional players for their Week 9 road matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs after downgrading Joseph Ossai, Nahshon Wright and VJ Payne to out on Saturday.

As New York (2-6) looks to snap a three-game losing streak against Kansas City (5-2), the organization made the changes to its latest injury report just one day before Sunday's contest.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported the updates Saturday on X, formerly known as Twitter.

Ossai's absence will affect New York's defensive front, while Wright's unavailability reduces the team's options in the secondary. Payne's absence further limits the Jets' available personnel as they attempt to turn their season around.

Jets face mounting challenges ahead of Week 9 matchup with Chiefs

The Jets now face another difficult challenge against a Chiefs team that has won five of its first seven games. Kansas City will look to capitalize on its home-field advantage while New York attempts to avoid falling further behind in the AFC standings.

With three more players officially ruled out, the Jets will need other members of their roster to step into larger roles against Kansas City.

New York will face the Chiefs on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS, hoping to end its losing streak and secure its third victory of the season.

articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers on Saturday officially activated wide receiver Demarcus Robinson from IR in time for the veteran wide receiver to suit up against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday.

In a corresponding move the 49ers placed WR Christian Kirk on IR after the receiver suffered a meniscus injury in practice leading up to Week 9. It's unclear whether Kirk will return this season, although the 49ers are rapidly running out of IR return designations so his season could be over by default depending on how other IR returns shake out.

This will mark Kirk's second IR stint of the year. He started the season there after suffering a calf injury in training camp. He was out until Week 7 when he returned vs. the Atlanta Falcons and didn't earn a target. Now he's on IR again where he'll be out at least four weeks.

Robinson also had his 'questionable' designation lifted. He's been out since suffering a high ankle sprain in Week 2 vs. the Miami Dolphins. His return gives quarterback Brock Purdy a reliable veteran WR in a receiving corps full of unproven options with Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel both ruled out.

With so many injuries at wide receiver, the 49ers also elevated recently-signed WR KhaDarel Hodge to their roster from the practice squad. It's a standard elevation so he'll revert back to the practice squad after Sunday's game. He appeared in three games for the 49ers before his release. San Francisco re-signed him after their Week 8 bye. Hodge has one catch for 18 yards in 2026.

articles.title: Grading Auburn football's comeback win against Arkansas: Report card
articles.summary: How good, or bad, was it for Auburn football in its comeback win against Arkansas? See our full report card to find out.
articles.body:
AUBURN — In its first eight games, Auburn football had a glimpse of what it was at its best, certainly when it upset top-ranked Georgia on the road. It found out what it truly looks like at its worst in Game 9, even if it won.

It was a 26-23 victory, as Auburn (5-4, 3-4 SEC) needed a comeback to beat Arkansas (3-6, 1-5), which entered the weekend with a single conference victory.

The comeback was thrilling, but the start was brutal. Here's a look at how we grade it, with a full report card for Auburn's performance against the Razorbacks.

Byrum Brown has magical capabilities, and Auburn's offense is seemingly incapable of rolling early. Both things have been true and remained as such against the Razorbacks, meaning the unit breaks even on the report card.

DJ Durkin's unit clamped down late in several aspects, but it struggled to stop one of the worst offenses in the SEC throughout. If not for the havoc it created, it would've surely been a failure.

For the second consecutive week, Auburn whiffed on a PAT and had a kickoff go out of bounds. That can't happen.

The offense looked like an entirely different team after halftime, but now nine games into this season and Alex Golesh's coaching staff still hasn't found an answer for persistent problems.

Auburn football final grade vs Arkansas : D

What happened against LSU and Ole Miss had at least one excuse, as Auburn was facing two uber-talented, successful squads. That wasn't present with the Razorbacks, even if Auburn secured the victory, casting a shadow on the result.

articles.title: 'When in doubt, find 45': Jelani Thurman matches UNC football record vs UConn
articles.summary: Tight end Jelani Thurman continues to show why he's such a weapon for UNC football. The Tar Heels saw it again in a record-matching game at UConn.
articles.body:
Check out our UNC football vs UConn photo gallery, best images

On a rainy, record-matching afternoon for tight end Jelani Thurman , quarterback Billy Edwards didn't want to describe it as a "big" performance.

"I don't want to say that big because that's what is expected of him," Edwards said in an interview on the CBS Sports Network after UNC football's 38-21 win at UConn .

"He's a dog. He's proved himself time and time again this season. Makes my job easier as a quarterback. When in doubt, find 45 and get him the ball. You saw what he was able to do with it."

No. 45 for the Tar Heels (5-4, 2-3 ACC) has eight touchdowns through nine games, matching the single-season record set by Mike Chatham in 1979. Thurman will have a chance to break that 47-year-old mark over the final three games of the regular season.

"I feel like that's just great preparation," Thurman said after hauling in seven catches for 64 yards and two touchdowns against the Huskies (4-5).

"My offense believing in me, my (offensive coordinator Bobby Petrino) believing in me, my team believing in me, my quarterback finding me, making great plays."

An Ohio State transfer with a 6-foot-6, 245-pound frame, Thurman has caught multiple TDs in three games since joining the Tar Heels. When asked during a postgame press conference what Thurman does for UNC's offense, Bill Belichick struggled to find a weakness.

"Just a really good player. He's got good length, he's fast, he's got really good hands, he's good running after the catch, he blocks well," Belichick said.

"You have to respect the running game behind him. He's good on catch-and-run plays and he's good down the field. It's almost impossible to overthrow him. He's got a great catch radius. We saw that last week (against Miami) on a touchdown catch in the back of the end zone. Yeah, he's done a great job for us."

As Thurman was wrapping up his interview with reporter Tiffany Blackmon, wide receiver Jordan Shipp and running back Demon June snuck up behind him, yelling his name and his number with smiles stretched across their faces.

Despite his individual success, Thurman was more elated about UNC's ability to put together a complete performance, which helped the Tar Heels exceed their win total from Belichick's debut season.

It also puts Thurman and his team within one victory of becoming bowl eligible.

"It feels good to actually come out here and get a win, put four quarters of football up, execute and just show the world what we got," Thurman said.

articles.title: Cross snatch late win over Gowna to progress in Ulster
articles.summary: Rian O'Neill's last-gasp score secures a 1-22 to 2-18 comeback win for Crossmaglen in their Ulster Club SFC quarter-final against Gowna at Breffni Park.
articles.body:
Rian O'Neill's last-gasp score secured a 1-22 to 2-18 comeback win for Crossmaglen in their Ulster Club SFC quarter-final against Gowna at Breffni Park.

Three two-pointers and a goal from Conor Madden had Gowna in command 1-13 to 1-5 at the break.

Seanie Hartin grabbed a second goal upon the restart, but Cross produced a seismic comeback as they did so often on their way to winning the Armagh championship.

Rian and Oisin O'Neill scored two-pointers to bridge the gap and an orange flag from Oisin brought them level on 56 minutes.

The lead changed hands thereafter with Ryan Donohue nudging Gowna back in front with a score from outside the arc of his own.

However, Cross and the O'Neill brothers would have the last say as Oisin played a two-point free short to Rian and he raised the roof and split the posts to send his club into the final four.

Cross fight back to secure place in last four

Oisin O'Neill opened the scoring for Cross inside the first 60 seconds, but they would have to wait 13 minutes before registering their second.

In that time, Gowna made hay. Cian Madden and Conor Brady got the Cavan champions going before Conor Casey shot back-to-back scores, while Fiachra Brady raised an orange flag to stretch their lead to five.

Rian O'Neill responded for Crossmaglen, but a free from Cian Madden and another two-pointer from Daire Madden had Gowna in full control.

A 20th-minute punch to the net from Conor Madden put the Breffni men nine points clear.

Casey landed Gowna's third two-pointer of the first half, but Cross did get themselves back to within eight by the break.

Rian O'Neill popped the ball inside to McConville, who slipped his marker and fired to the net.

The south Armagh outfit trailed 1-13 to 1-5 at the break, and when Seanie Hartin netted in the first minute of the second half, the deficit opened up to 11.

However, the 11-time Ulster champions rallied and hit seven unanswered points, with Rian and Oisin O'Neill both nailing two-point efforts.

By the 57th minute, the Armagh champions were ahead when lively substitute Seamus Teelan put them in front for the first time since the opening stages.

Still, there was time for Ryan Donohue to raise an orange flag and put Gowna's noses back in front but Rian O'Neill's kick in the dying embers snatched the victory for Cross.
