articles.title: Eagles Week 9 injury report vs. Giants: Saquon Barkley still battling through hamstring issue
articles.summary: Saquon Barkley is preparing to face his former team, but the Philadelphia Eagles running back is not entering Week 9 with a clean bill of health. Barkley con...
articles.body:
Saquon Barkley is preparing to face his former team, but the Philadelphia Eagles running back is not entering Week 9 with a clean bill of health. Barkley continues to manage hamstring and back injuries after missing Wednesday's practice and participating on a limited basis Thursday and Friday.

The encouraging development for Philadelphia is his game status. Barkley received no injury designation and is available for Sunday's matchup against the New York Giants . His restricted practice schedule reflects ongoing injury management rather than an official questionable or doubtful designation.

That distinction matters for an Eagles offense missing several receiving options. Philadelphia has ruled out six players, including DeVonta Smith , Dontayvion Wicks and Britain Covey, while quarterback Tanner McKee remains questionable. Barkley's availability offers some stability amid another challenging week of personnel adjustments.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Saquon Barkley cleared to play despite lingering injuries

Barkley's practice progression followed a familiar pattern: time off early in the week, followed by limited work as the Eagles prepared for another divisional matchup. He has continued playing through the hamstring and back issues, including last Sunday's loss at Washington, when he scored a rushing touchdown.

His production against the Commanders illustrated both his value and the limitations surrounding Philadelphia's ground game. Barkley finished with 13 carries for 30 yards and a touchdown, adding a 24-yard reception. Those numbers followed a seven-carry, 62-yard performance against Dallas in Week 7.

Through six appearances this season, Barkley has accumulated 274 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 56 attempts. His 4.9-yard average shows he can still produce efficiently overall, but his recent workloads have been considerably smaller than the volume associated with his most productive Philadelphia stretch.

For perspective, Barkley rushed for 2,005 yards during his first Eagles season in 2024 and followed that with 1,140 yards in 2025. This year's interrupted availability has made establishing that same rhythm more difficult.

The Giants matchup adds a familiar opponent, but the central issue is workload rather than sentiment. Clearance to play does not establish how many touches Barkley will receive or whether Philadelphia will distribute more opportunities elsewhere. The final injury report confirms availability, not an unrestricted role.

Eagles rule out six as other injured starters progress

Smith's hamstring injury and Wicks' ankle issue leave Philadelphia without two important receivers. Covey is also out with a knee injury. All three missed every practice this week, limiting the offense's receiving depth before Sunday's game.

The remaining confirmed absences are linebacker Jihaad Campbell, who has hamstring and quadriceps injuries, defensive back Michael Carter II, who is dealing with an abdomen injury, and cornerback Jonathan Jones, who has a hamstring issue. Each recorded three consecutive missed practices.

McKee's rib injury remains another situation to monitor. He practiced fully Wednesday before being limited Thursday and Friday and carries the Eagles' lone questionable designation. Philadelphia has already announced that Joe Milton will start against New York.

Elsewhere, kicker Jake Elliott and outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard advanced from limited participation to full practices Friday. Jalyx Hunt remained limited throughout the week with knee and ankle injuries but received no game designation.

Zack Baun, Markel Bell, Jordan Davis, Landon Dickerson, Dallas Goedert, Kenny Moore II and Moro Ojomo practiced fully throughout the supplied report. Jordan Mailata's listed sessions were also full, although his Friday entry is missing. None carries a listed game designation, providing encouragement around an otherwise depleted roster.

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton opens up on clear-the-air talks with Charles Leclerc after Mexican GP clash
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton has confirmed he and Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc have cleared the air following their clash at the Mexican GP
articles.body:
Lewis Hamilton has opened up on the clear-the-air chat he had with his Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc ahead of the Brazilian Grand Prix.

The Ferrari team-mates clashed on the opening lap of the Mexican Grand Prix last weekend. Leclerc attempted to overtake the seven-time champion, who had started from pole position. Both drivers ran wide during the move, with Leclerc rejoining the track in the lead.

Hamilton dropped to third behind Max Verstappen as a result, and Leclerc was handed a five-second penalty for the incident.

After the race, Hamilton was furious with how hard Leclerc had raced him and called for serious talks within the team.

The Briton was asked about the discussions after a rain-soaked qualifying session for the Brazilian Grand Prix.

"Fred [Vasseur] hasn't cleared the air in the sense of me and Charles. We sat and spoke and we squashed it and we're moving on," Hamilton said when asked by Sky Sports F1 whether team principal Vasseur had managed to patch things up between the two drivers.

"I think we still have a huge amount of respect for each other. And I'm glad we had a chat. Now we move on along just fine as normal. So sometimes in those scenarios, it just takes having a conversation and there's been no demands from either side.

"It's just been both giving our points and areas that we can do better and support each other. So I'm hoping to have better races moving forward."

Both Hamilton and Leclerc are taking grid penalties for the Brazilian Grand Prix. Hamilton will start at the back of the grid due to his Ferrari being fitted with a new power unit, while Leclerc will start from 14th due to a 10-place grid penalty for a new internal combustion engine.

The Brazilian Grand Prix will take place on Sunday 8 November at 2pm local time (5pm UK time).

articles.title: Dylan Larkin Trade Rumor: Bruins Veteran and Draft Pick Floated in Potential Red Wings Deal
articles.summary: A source has floated Pavel Zacha, Mason Lohrei or a draft pick in a potential Dylan Larkin trade with Boston. Would Detroit accept?
articles.body:
The Dylan Larkin trade saga has taken another interesting turn, and the Boston Bruins remain a team worth watching.

While the Detroit Red Wings continue searching for an acceptable return for their former captain, a source has floated a potential trade framework involving veteran center Pavel Zacha , defenseman Mason Lohrei , or a first-round draft pick.

There is a catch, of course. Actually, there are several.

According to reporting from James Murphy of The Sick Podcast , Boston has been pushing harder to enter the Larkin sweepstakes. However, the Bruins reportedly have no interest in surrendering prized young center James Hagens, a player Detroit is believed to covet.

That raises an obvious question: Could Boston satisfy the Red Wings without sacrificing one of its most promising young players?

A Potential Dylan Larkin Trade Framework Involving Pavel Zacha

Murphy's reporting included an intriguing suggestion from an NHL source regarding what Boston might offer instead of Hagens.

The source wondered whether Zacha, accompanied by Lohrei or a first-round selection, could provide enough value to get Detroit interested.

Importantly, this was a hypothetical framework raised by a source, not confirmation that Boston has submitted such an offer .

Zacha, 29, is an established NHL center who could immediately help fill the enormous hole Larkin would leave behind. He also carries some risk, considering he is scheduled to become an unrestricted free agent following the 2026-27 season.

Detroit would presumably want some assurance that Zacha would remain beyond this season before considering him a significant piece of the return.

Lohrei presents a different kind of opportunity. The young defenseman could potentially become part of Detroit's long-term blue line, while a first-round pick would offer additional flexibility as the organization evaluates its future.

But would Zacha and one additional asset really be enough?

The Red Wings are in an uncomfortable position, but that does not mean they should accept a disappointing return simply to end the drama.

As we previously explained when examining a different hypothetical Bruins trade involving Larkin , Detroit must evaluate not just the number of assets coming back, but whether those pieces can meaningfully improve the franchise.

Larkin is 30 years old and remains under contract through the 2030-31 season with an $8.7 million annual cap hit.

That is a significant commitment for any acquiring team, but it also means Detroit would be surrendering an established center with several years remaining on his contract.

Zacha could help immediately. Lohrei could provide longer-term upside. A first-round pick would be valuable.

But none individually replaces what Larkin has provided.

And if Boston refuses to include Hagens, Detroit should seriously consider whether another team can offer a more attractive package.

Of course, there is another rather important problem.

Boston reportedly remains outside Larkin's list of acceptable trade destinations.

According to The Hockey News' November 6 roundup , the Red Wings have been unable to find a satisfactory deal among Larkin's approved destinations and would prefer that he expand his list.

And as we previously covered when examining the potential Thanksgiving turning point in Larkin's trade standoff , both sides appear unwilling to make significant concessions.

Boston might have the assets to interest Detroit.

But until Larkin approves the Bruins as a destination, any proposed package remains academic.

For now, the Zacha scenario offers another look at what a potential Boston deal might involve.

The bigger question is whether Detroit would be getting enough in return to justify finally moving on from Larkin.

And that's a question Shawn Horcoff cannot afford to get wrong.

articles.title: Anthony Davis Reportedly Wants To Return To Lakers, But A Reunion Is Unlikely
articles.summary: Anthony Davis apparently wants to be a Laker again, but it's unlikely that wish will come true.
articles.body:
Washington Wizards star Anthony Davis spent five and a half seasons with the Los Angeles Lakers , and it appears he might want a reunion. Brian Windhorst recently appeared on ESPN LA's The Sedano & Kap Morning Show , where co-host Scott Kaplan told him he'd overheard reporters in the media room at a Lakers game talking about Davis wanting to come back to Los Angeles.

"They don't realize I'm listening and I'm hearing what they're saying," Kaplan said. "[One of them said], 'I hear that Anthony Davis wants to return to the Lakers.'… I think they're credentialized. I think they know what they're talking about. They assume I have no idea. But Windy, could Anthony Davis… We always talk about another big man for the Lakers.

"A, have you heard it?" Kaplan continued. "And B, is there a world where that could happen?"

Windhorst rightly pointed out that Kaplan was talking about gossip in the press room. As for whether Davis and the Lakers could reunite, the 48-year-old doesn't see it happening.

"Very unlikely," Windhorst said. "Anthony Davis is one of the bigger question marks in the league this year. There's like three guys we're watching, sort of star-level players about will they get traded. One is Anthony Davis, one is Kyrie Irving, Domantas Sabonis is on there. All of them are in the same boat.

"All of them have options in their contract for next season," Windhorst continued. "… The Wizards basically said, 'We want to see Anthony Davis play 20 to 30 games, see how he fits with our group, and then we're going to revisit about whether we want to give him a contract extension.' Obviously, if they give him a contract extension, he agrees to it, he's not being traded.

"If he doesn't get a contract extension, then I think you're going to see his name out there on the trade market," Windhorst added. "But here's the thing. The Lakers just don't have much high-value things, forget about Anthony Davis, just for any star player. They just don't have much to trade. They've traded all of their picks, for the most part."

Even if we ignore the lack of assets aspect for a bit, Davis is making $58.4 million in 2026-27. The Lakers won't be trading Luka Doncic , Austin Reaves , or Walker Kessler to the Wizards for him, which makes matching salaries a very difficult task. They only have three other players making over $10 million in 2026-27: Quentin Grimes , Sandro Mamukelashvili , and Jarred Vanderbilt . Their combined salary is $39.3 million.

The Lakers would have to give up most of their quality role players to get to $58 million. Even if they decide to do that, the Wizards would then have to see enough value in those players to send Davis to Los Angeles.

The Lakers also gave up two first-round picks and two first-round pick swaps to get Kessler from the Utah Jazz in the summer, so a 2032 first-round pick swap is the only valuable draft asset they can include in a package. So, you struggle to see a trade here.

Another route you'd think of would be Davis declining his $62.8 million player option for 2027-28 and joining the Lakers as a free agent. The issue there would be that he'd have to take a massive pay cut, and he reportedly wants a near-max contract . You just don't see an avenue.

Now, would Davis be a good fit with the Lakers? Absolutely. The 10-time All-Star always spoke about the Lakers needing to add a starting center during his time there so that he could play power forward. Well, Kessler is there now, so Davis, an NBA champion with the Lakers in 2020, won't have to play center. The 33-year-old would also address some of their defensive woes.

Davis, whom the Lakers traded to the Dallas Mavericks for Doncic in February 2025, is averaging 23.4 points, 9.3 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.4 steals, and 1.1 blocks per game for the Wizards in 2026-27. He is still playing at a high level, but injuries remain a concern. That's just another reason why the Lakers probably shouldn't be interested in a reunion.

articles.title: Saints make surprising Kendre Miller decision despite RB concerns
articles.summary: The New Orleans Saints have released running back Kendre Miller ahead of their Week 9 matchup against the Cleveland Browns, leaving the organization with li...
articles.body:
The New Orleans Saints have released running back Kendre Miller ahead of their Week 9 matchup against the Cleveland Browns , leaving the organization with limited options in the backfield amid several injuries.

Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reported the surprising roster decision Saturday on X, formerly known as Twitter.

"The Saints released Kendre Miller, per source," Underhill reported.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The move comes as New Orleans (2-5) prepares to host Cleveland (5-3) on Sunday , with the Saints already dealing with significant injuries at running back.

Veteran Travis Etienne Jr. remains on injured reserve with a hamstring injury, while CJ Donaldson has been ruled out for Sunday's contest due to a shoulder injury and concussion.

Those absences, combined with Miller's release, leave Alvin Kamara and Audric Estime as the Saints' only two available running backs entering the matchup.

Miller, 24, appeared in six games this season, recording 159 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 57 carries, averaging just 2.8 yards per attempt. He also contributed nine receptions for 37 yards.

The former third-round pick out of TCU struggled to establish consistency throughout the season despite receiving increased opportunities.

Saints face uncertainty at running back ahead of Browns matchup

In New Orleans' Week 6 victory over the New York Giants, Miller recorded a season-high 70 rushing yards on 20 carries. However, he followed that performance with just six rushing yards on eight attempts during the Saints' 16-10 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris .

Across four seasons with New Orleans, Miller appeared in 27 games, totaling 656 rushing yards and five touchdowns on 184 carries. He also recorded 29 receptions for 217 yards.

Miller's departure raises additional questions about the Saints' offensive depth as head coach Kellen Moore looks to get the organization back on track following its Week 8 bye.

With Etienne sidelined and Donaldson unavailable, Kamara and Estime could see increased responsibilities against Cleveland.

The decision also ends Miller's tenure with the organization after New Orleans selected him with the No. 71 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft.

The Saints will attempt to rebound from their Week 7 loss to Pittsburgh when they host the Browns on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS.

articles.title: Mestemaker and Hawkins lead Oklahoma State's dominant effort over Kansas State
articles.summary: (AP) — Drew Mestemaker became the first Bowl Subdivision player with four touchdown passes, one rushing touchdown and one receiving touchdown since Virginia’...
articles.body:
MANHATTAN, Kan. (AP) — Drew Mestemaker became the first Bowl Subdivision player with four touchdown passes, one rushing touchdown and one receiving touchdown since Virginia's Brennan Armstrong against BYU in 2021 as Oklahoma State trounced Kansas State 66-28 on Saturday.

Mestemaker, who finished 22-of-28 passing for 313 yards, had three first-half touchdown passes, and Caleb Hawkins had three first-half rushing touchdowns for the Cowboys.

Hawkins rushed for 175 yards with three rushing touchdowns and added a receiving touchdown for Oklahoma State (6-3, 4-2 Big 12).

Kansas State dropped its third straight game to fall to 4-5, 1-5.

After forcing a three-and-out on K-State's first possession, Oklahoma State went 72 yards on three plays to take the early lead. Mestemaker hit Justin Bowick for a 32-yard touchdown.

Kansas State answered with its own three-play drive, with 73 of the 77 yards coming on a TD pass from Blake Barnett to Derrick Salley behind busted coverage.

Hawkins' 21-yard touchdown run gave the lead back to the Cowboys. Hawkins then raced 37 yards for another score, putting him at 96 rushing yards with 5 minutes left in the first quarter.

Mestemaker hit Morgan McPhaul for a 3-yard touchdown to extend the lead to 28-7. His first mistake was a pick-6 made by Logan Bartley.

Mestemaker ran it in from the 1-yard line to stretch the lead to 35-14, and Hawkins' third touchdown of the half made it 42-14. Mestemaker then found Miles Coleman on a 19-yard touchdown with 11 seconds left in the half for a 49-14 lead.

In the third quarter, Mestemaker added a 5-yard TD pass to Hawkins and then caught a 5-yard TD from Wyatt Young.

Oklahoma State: The Cowboys' offense was humming from the start. They were driving for their 28-7 first-quarter lead when they faced their first third down.

Kansas State: The Wildcats allowed touchdowns on OSU's first six red-zone possessions.

Oklahoma State: returns home next Saturday to host Texas Tech.

Kansas State: plays at TCU next Saturday.

articles.title: Mercer defeats Chattanooga 14-7 in overtime on Pickles' TD pass to Smith
articles.summary: (AP) — JP Pickles threw two touchdown passes to Brayden Smith, the second one for the lead in overtime, and Mercer held on to defeat Chattanooga 14-7 on Satu...
articles.body:
CHATTANOOGA, Tenn. (AP) — JP Pickles threw two touchdown passes to Brayden Smith, the second one for the lead in overtime, and Mercer held on to defeat Chattanooga 14-7 on Saturday.

Mercer, the 14th-ranked team in the Stats Perform FCS Top 25, had the ball first in overtime and on the fifth play Pickles found Smith in the end zone for a 7-yard score.

On Chattanooga's OT possession, Mercer's Mike Polke recovered a fumble by Battle Alberson to end the game.

The Mocs, ranked No. 25 by Stats Perform, scored first on Alberson's 4-yard run but finished the first half with only 117 yards on offense and three first downs. Journey Wyche's 50-yard run that set up the touchdown accounted for all but 67 yards of the Mocs' first-half output.

It was 7-7 at halftime, Mercer's score coming on a 3-yard pass from Pickles to Smith.

Mercer's Simon Zeidan missed three field goals in regulation, the last coming from 42 yards out on the last play of the fourth quarter.

Pickles completed 13 of 22 passes for 110 yards and added 73 yards rushing. Zahmari Palode-Gary led the Bears with 96 yards on the ground.

Mercer (8-2, 5-1 Southern Conference) outgained Chattanooga (6-4, 5-2) in total yards, 340-264. Wyche had 106 yards rushing for the Mocs.

The Bears have won nine of their last 11 road games, including nine in a row against FCS opponents.

Mercer: at Tennessee Tech next Saturday. ___

articles.title: Mason McCormick wasn't fined for dumping Jared Verse on his head
articles.summary: Browns defensive end Jared Verse is getting upset.
articles.body:
Browns defensive end Jared Verse is getting upset.

Verse, who was miffed at being dumped on his head by Steelers guard Mason McCormick on an extra-point try last Sunday — and at his teammates for not rushing to his defense , will surely be unhappy to learn that the NFL didn't fine McCormick for his WWE move.

McCormick was flagged for unnecessary roughness on the play.

It's unclear why the league didn't fine McCormick. The league never explains the basis for not imposing a financial penalty on a given player.

Regardless, the league was as unbothered by the play as the other Browns players were. And it's likely that Verse will have something to say about it after Sunday's game at the Saints.

articles.title: Arch Manning, No. 7 Texas rally for win over No. 18 Missouri, avoid letdown on road
articles.summary: The Longhorns didn't take their first lead until late in the fourth quarter, and Texas' defense applied the finishing touches on a crucial win over the Tiger...
articles.body:
COLUMBIA, Mo. - In his finest game of the season, Arch Manning threw for 297 yards and three touchdowns, two of them to his running backs, to lead seventh-ranked Texas to a 34-20 win over No. 18 Missouri on Saturday afternoon.

Manning's 28-yard TD pass to Raleek Brown with 5:03 left gave Texas its first lead of the game.

The Longhorns (7-2, 4-2 SEC) then hold off the Tigers' (6-3, 3-3) in the final two minutes to seal the win. Warren Roberson forced a fumble by Cayden Lee that Graceson Little returned to the Missouri 6. Brown then scored on an 8-yard run to put the game out of reach.

The third quarter produced no certainty about the outcome but plenty of fireworks. The two teams scored four times in five offensive possessions and the Tigers missed a 46-yard field goal on the only other series of the period.

Missouri seemingly had the biggest play of the game when Naeshaun Montgomery caught a short 8-yard pass in the right flat against a blitzing defense and shrugged off would-be tackler Jelani McDonald to take it 72 yards for the go-ahead touchdown and a 20-13 lead.

The sophomore receiver's first touchdown of his career also marked the longest gainer of the year against the Longhorns and the first 50-yard-plus play by a Texas opponent all season.

However, the Longhorns responded with a curious scoring drive of their own. Aided by a pass interference call against Missouri and a review that went Texas' way and rewarded it with a 16-yard gain on a fumble recovery by Emmett Mosley V when Missouri thought it had a sack or an incompletion.

Jermaine Bishop Jr. gathered in a 25-yard touchdown pass on a Missouri busted assignment allowing the freshman receiver to run free for the second score of his career and a 20-20 tie.

Texas and Missouri swapped field goal after field goal although Missouri botched two of its. Each had a field goal in the third quarter, but the Tigers missed their second of the game after Ryan Niblett's fumble on a kickoff.

The game was knotted at 10-10 at intermission after the two teams traded field goals. Texas was fortunate that Missouri's Blake Craig pushed a 38-yard field goal wide right midway through the second quarter.

Gianni Spetic, who has missed just one field goal in his first 14 attempts with a 53-yard wide right against Oklahoma, booted his fifth straight on a 27-yarder. That followed a blocked punt by linebacker Jonathan Cunningham - Alex January blocked an Ole Miss field goal this year - and set up a 30-yard drive highlighted by a 22-yard pass to Ryan Wingo.

Missouri surprisingly came out flinging the ball despite a stout running game that has produced 12 touchdowns. Austin Simmons threw 21 passes in the first half and completed a 2-yard out pattern to Brett Norfleet for a touchdown on the Tigers' opening drive of the game.

Texas' offense sputtered for much of the first half but had a credible running attack behind Brown and scored its only touchdown on a perfectly executed reverse screen pass to Derek Cooper for 24 yards.

articles.title: Elaina Lucido, Maverick DeLaRosa net Top 10 finishes at UIL State Meet
articles.summary: Elaina Lucido posted her best finish at the UIL State Cross Country Meet and Maverick DeLaRosa also finished Top 10. See results for the Coastal Bend.
articles.body:
Carroll's Elaina Lucido capped a stellar four years of running cross country for the Tigers with her best UIL state meet finish in three trips to Round Rock, crossing in seventh place in the Class 5A girls race at Old Settlers Park.

Lucido's time of 18:21.6 was good for her best finish at the state meet, four places better than in 2025.

Santa Gertrudis Academy's Maverick DeLaRosa was making his first appearance at the state meet, and also netted a Top 10 finish.

The Lions senior finished ninth in the Class 3A boys race with a time of 16:09.1.

Veterans Memorial's Trey Llanes ran a 15:46.1 in the Class 5A boys division to finish 15th overall and lead the Eagles in a 10th place finish in the final team standings.
